summary.title: LongHorizon-Harness: Advancing Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Tasks

details: In existing agent harnesses, task execution, task-state tracking, and completion assessment all live in one continuously growing context, so state becomes hard to track and the agent's own (possibly wrong) self-assessments propagate into later decisions.
Reformulates long-horizon execution as a task-state management problem rather than a single long trajectory.
LongHorizon-Harness: a harness that maintains the task state explicitly outside execution and advances it only with facts independently verified from the environment.

Manage-Execute-Audit loop: a manager (no environment access) keeps structured state records (requirements/artifacts/facts with status and evidence) and emits one bounded subtask contract with acceptance criteria; a fresh-context executor performs only that subtask and its raw trajectory is discarded; a read-only auditor independently inspects the resulting environment to certify completion and integrity. Executor claims never update state directly; audit reports are the only cross-round memory.

A lightweight AgentAdapter lets any existing agent backend (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenClaw, ...) fill each role without modifying its native agent loop, with role-specific tool/permission boundaries (GUI vs CLI).
WeaveBench (114 tasks, coupled GUI+CLI workflows, 8 domains): PassRate (score >= 0.8) and mean Overall score, official judge (Claude Opus 4.7 trajectory-aware).
OSWorld 2.0 (108 professional desktop tasks, ~1.6h median human time, official osworld-v2-2026.06.24 Docker VMs): Binary accuracy (score = 1) and Partial (mean score); plus a 34-task Opus 4.7 subset.
Terminal-Bench 2.1 (pure CLI, Harbor + Docker backend, hidden tests): average over 3 runs per task, 5h per-trial timeout.
Primary backbone Qwen 3.7-Plus, with Claude Opus 4.7 (and GPT-5.6 Luna with Codex on Terminal-Bench) for generality.
Manager, executor, and auditor all instantiated with the same backbone so the comparison isolates the state-management layer.
Execution backend held fixed as Claude Code (specific pinned versions) in the matched comparisons.
Per-round budgets: executor 1800s, manager and auditor 300s each; maximum 25 MEA rounds per task.

GUI tools: standard screenshot + pyautogui actuation, plus a restricted save_screenshot evidence tool; CLI role gets shell/file/coding/test capabilities. On OSWorld a hybrid GUI+CLI tool pool is used (baselines are GUI-only).
High reasoning effort / thinking enabled, max_tokens 65,536; screenshots proxied as image URLs; OSWorld human-in-the-loop tasks answered by the native user simulator.
Matched baseline: the same backbone running in the plain Claude Code harness (or official single-action mode on OSWorld).

Reference (unmatched) points: officially reported WeaveBench results for Claude Opus 4.7 / GPT-5.5 / Gemini / Qwen with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Codex CLI; OSWorld 2.0 official batched/single-action leaderboard; Terminal-Bench 2.1 official leaderboard.
Token accounting decomposed by role (manager / executor / auditor) and cost-performance frontier vs. output tokens per task.

Breakdowns by WeaveBench domain, OSWorld capability tag, Terminal-Bench category/difficulty/tag; paired same-task trajectory case studies; 17-task WeaveBench Games subset compared per task across both backbones.

key_findings.finding: Externalizing and independently auditing task state yields large gains on long-horizon tasks under matched model and execution backend.
key_findings.evidence: With Qwen 3.7-Plus and Claude Code as executor backend: WeaveBench PassRate 51.8% -> 80.7% (Overall 0.702 -> 0.835) with improvements in all eight domains; Terminal-Bench 2.1 69.7% -> 77.2%; OSWorld 2.0 binary 2.8% -> 8.3% and partial 21.5% -> 35.2%. The WeaveBench result also far exceeds the best officially reported 41.2% (Claude Opus 4.7 + Claude Code).

key_findings.finding: The gains are complementary to backbone strength rather than a compensation for weak models, and a stronger harness with a weaker model can beat a stronger model with a plain harness.
key_findings.evidence: On the 34-task OSWorld 2.0 subset, Claude Opus 4.7 improves from 20.6% to 35.3% binary and 55.8% to 66.9% partial. On the 17-task WeaveBench Games subset, mean score rises 0.680 -> 0.809 for Opus and 0.524 -> 0.733 for Qwen; Qwen with the harness (0.733) exceeds Opus with base Claude Code (0.680).

key_findings.finding: The mechanism mainly raises the failure floor by recovering trajectories that would otherwise end in near-total failure.
key_findings.evidence: All six WeaveBench Games tasks where the Qwen baseline scored <= 0.04 recover to 0.30-0.92 (e.g., pokerth_equity_play 0.00 -> 0.92, stockfish_puzzle 0.00 -> 0.55); domain analysis shows largest PassRate gains where baselines were weakest (Design +60 pp, Spatial/3D +50 pp) and only +5.6 pp for the already-strong Desktop domain; Terminal-Bench gains are larger on hard tasks (+0.122) than medium (+0.042).

key_findings.finding: Overhead is dominated by auditing, not state management, and total cost is not a fixed multiplier but depends on model capability and required recovery rounds.
key_findings.evidence: Manager consumes only 2.8% / 2.0% / 8.1% of tokens on WeaveBench / OSWorld / Terminal-Bench versus 19.4% / 24.8% / 38.1% for the auditor; total cost is 2.3x baseline on WeaveBench, 3.6x output tokens on OSWorld (28.9K -> 104K per task), but 24% fewer tokens on Terminal-Bench. On the Games subset the harness raises Qwen from 10.7M to 34.3M tokens per task yet reduces Opus from 16.5M to 11.1M.

key_findings.finding: Benefits are governed by whether a task's bottleneck is long-horizon execution reliability versus a single-step model capability, independent of GUI vs CLI interface.
key_findings.evidence: Largest improvements occur where progress maps to durable verifiable artifacts (Terminal-Bench system-administration 0.593 -> 0.889, images tag +0.833, version-control +0.333; OSWorld streaming-interaction 0.000 -> 0.500, human-in-the-loop +0.332), while categories dominated by individual capabilities or hidden grading semantics regress (data-science -0.125, mathematics -0.167, video-processing -0.333). Case studies show audits catching plausible-but-noncompliant completions (XML-edited headings scoring 0.00 -> 0.89 via the prescribed GUI workflow) and state records freeing later executors from a stalled 400-step GUI retry loop (0.59 -> 0.92).
